verified_findings: TRAINING AXES (verifier-confirmed OLS + matched pairs on leaderboard.txt best-checkpoint stall_score; I re-read the leaderboard values). Five axes move the validation stall score beyond replicate noise, not three: event fraction p, rollout horizon K, initialisation (scratch +0.46 to +0.52 m/s), learning rate 1e-4 (hurts: +0.21 at p.6/K80, +0.09 at p.3/K40) and dropout (hurts: +0.30 / +0.51 for 0.1 / 0.2). p and K act as thresholds, not doses: p>0 is a step of about -0.19 m/s (0->0.3: -0.16/-0.24/-0.16 at K8/40/80) that saturates by 0.3 (0.3->0.6: +0.09/-0.03/+0.06; 0.6->0.9: -0.01/-0.05 while rejected-feasible routes rise 59->89 and 93->199); K acts as a step between 40 and 80 (8->40: +0.05/-0.03/-0.15; 40->80: -0.33/-0.25/-0.16; 80->120 +0.04; 80->160 -0.05). The progress loss interacts with the operating point: -0.22 at (p.6,K80) (0.97->0.75; replicated by ds->progvx -0.28, vx5->progvx -0.23; v_recov 0.71->0.39, v_match 0.75->0.45) but +0.21 at (p.3,K40) (1.16->1.37); the two points differ in both p and K so the moderator is not identified. Delta-scale, vx weight 5, progress weight 3, weight decay 0.5, context noise and matched-x3 weighting are within +/-0.06 of their matched baselines. Not null: the data mix (-0.01 at p.6/K80/prog but -0.22 at p.3/K40/prog) and the 'combo' (0.91/0.84/0.89 vs the primary's seeds 0.75/0.76/0.77, i.e. +0.09 to +0.16, attributable to its dropout component). A step-dummy fit with the progress x horizon interaction has residual sd 0.055 (R2 0.976) versus 0.12 for the linear OLS, so the linear model's residual is lack of fit, not noise.

WHAT THE IMAGINATION LEARNED (recomputed here from imagine_f105/rows.json + wp7_cache_v1/labels.json on the 52 f105 layouts with a feasible route: 451 feasible / 63 timeout / 36 stall / 31 contact routes under my categorisation, contact counted first). Closed-loop acceptance of stall routes barely moved: frozen 31/36, wp8_p6_k80_prog 31/36, _s1 27/36, wp8b_k120_p9 20/36 (minimum over the 40 runs 0.56; the analysts' categorisation gives 0.59). What fell is acceptance of timeout routes (frozen 63/63, wp7_ft 55/63, primary 39/63, p3_k80 24/63, k120_p9 16/63) and of feasible routes (428, 392, 370, 252 of 451). The imagined time on ACCEPTED feasible routes is unbiased for every model (mean -0.36/-0.19/+0.20 s vs Chrono, median ratio 0.98 for frozen/primary/k120_p9); the notes' '1.6 s / 6.9 s slower' is the mean over all 451 feasible routes and comes entirely from the rejected ones sitting at the 30 s imagined timeout. Rejection reasons for the primary: 90 of 95 are 'not completed at 30 s', 4 attitude/off-route, 1 collision (analyst, unverified). False rejections are layout-clustered: x_hill1_h180 (camera heading estimate flipped 176.8 deg per start_poses.json; all 13 routes Chrono-feasible) is rejected wholesale by every model, inflating every rej_feas count by 13 (frozen 23 is really 10); s_hill4_crater7_t+60_sh (pose error 1.5 deg, 9/9 feasible) is rejected 7/9 by the primary, 9/9 by p9_k80_prog and p3_k80, 3/9 by match3ap2, 0/9 by the frozen model - a genuine imagination failure on a correct pose (verified here).

PICK AND GATE (verifier-confirmed; gate distribution and sealed table recomputed here). Own-pick feasible counts span 31-43 of 52 over the 40 runs (mean 38.8; frozen 39; Spearman with stall_score -0.07, with rej_feas -0.08). Ranking each model's accepted set by Chrono's true cost gives 50/50, 51/51, 50/50, 48/48, 50/50 (frozen, primary, p9, p3_k80, match3ap2) - but accept-everything + oracle ranking also gives 52/52, so this does not isolate ranking from the gate. Own-pick losses to gate+fastest are 6/6/4/8/7; most are slow accepted candidates (v2-v4) that the imagination completes as a normal crossing while Chrono stalls or times out (recurrent: x_crater9_h090, all five pick v3/v4 which time out while v8 passes in 14.4 s; x_hill3_h000_sh, four of five pick v2/v4 while v5-v9 pass in 7.1-7.8 s), but 1-2 per model are layouts where everything was rejected (x_hill1_h180; s_hill4_crater7_t+60_sh for p9/p3_k80), won by the gate only through the no-model fallback, and contacts account for 3/3/2/4/3 of the 13/11/9/13/13 own-pick failures. The gate's false-accept rate is 2-3x higher on slow routes (v<=4: 25-33 %) than fast ones (v>=5: 10-15 %). Ranking accepted routes by imagined time alone (energy weight 0) recovers 74 % of the summed own-to-gate gap over 42 runs (better on 36, equal 4, worse 2) but does so by collapsing onto 'fastest accepted' (mean commanded speed 4.8-5.0 m/s), i.e. by re-injecting the bank's speed prior (v2 18/42 = 43 % feasible vs v8 50/58 = 86 %). Gate+fastest on f105 (recomputed here, all candidates eligible by mean_speed, fallback = heuristic): heuristic 44/52 (failures: 4 contact, 2 stall, 2 timeout); distribution over the 40 runs 43:1, 44:12, 45:23, 46:3, 47:1; wp8_p6_k80_prog 47 (fixes f_04, s_hill3_hill1_t-60_sh, x_hill3_h180; 0 breaks), its seeds 45/45, wp7_ft_mix_amd 45 (= the median ablation run), frozen 44. With only speed-coded candidates eligible: 43:1, 44:19, 45:19, 46:1 (primary 46). Exchangeable per-layout null: E[max of 40] = 46.5, P(max >= 47) = 0.49; 3 fixes / 0 breaks is sign-test p = 0.25. The fixes are not stall reproduction: s_hill3_hill1_t-60_sh (fixed by 18 of 40 runs) is a contact failure of the heuristic whose seq_v8_8 the models reject as an imagined timeout while also rejecting 6-8 of the 8 feasible routes there; x_hill3_h180 (9 runs) counts only because detour_R becomes eligible. Structural compression: P(2nd-fastest feasible | fastest feasible) = 42/44 on f105 and 83/86 sealed, so 187 false rejections of the fastest broke the pick only twice; the fallback is worth +1.6 layouts (without it the 40 runs average 43.2 and only 2 beat the heuristic); a random rejecter at matched rate scores 43.9 +/- 0.7 (P(>=44) 0.80). Sealed f106+f107 (recomputed here from imagine_sealed/rows.json + wp7_cache_sealed/labels.json, 93 layouts): heuristic 86 (7 failures, 3 contact-only); own picks primary/s1/s2/p9/p3_k80 76/77/79/81/80, frozen 80; gate+fastest 85/85/87/86/87 (fixes/breaks 0/1, 0/1, 1/0, 0/0, 1/0), frozen 86 - pooled 2 fixes / 2 breaks, mean 0.0 vs the heuristic. All 7 sealed failure layouts and all 8 f105 failure layouts have a feasible slower alternative (oracle gate 93/93, 52/52).

LOCAL TESTS VERSUS CLOSED LOOP (verifier-confirmed over the 40 runs' analyze_f105.txt). At their best runs the teacher-forced tests roughly doubled (stop predicted 0.25->0.55, in-stall hold 0.39->0.78, launch held 0.38->0.78; ~1.5-1.6x for the average run) but their correlation with closed-loop completion of stall routes is almost entirely overall pessimism: stall-route completion tracks feasible-route completion (r = +0.81, stall_done = 1.54 F_done - 0.76) and the residual correlations are -0.09 (S_pre), -0.21 (L_pre), -0.08 (hold). The tracker-in-the-loop pre-stop test is the most related local number (-0.83 with stop-route completion, residual -0.46, bank Youden J +0.69 vs +0.45/+0.51) but it is pessimism-laden too (-0.71 with feasible completion; the same test on feasible routes predicts stop completion at -0.74) and gives no advantage on launch failures (-0.56 vs -0.53). No f105 local number, including closed-loop stop completion itself, predicts the planner's pick outcome (r = +0.02 with own pick and with gate+fastest). Trade-off: wp8_p3_k80 has the best separation (stalled completion 0.40 vs feasible 0.87, balanced rejecter accuracy 0.71) and wp8b_k120_p9 rejects most (0.19/0.62) but also 199/451 feasible routes; wp8_p6_k80_prog (0.59/0.92) is the only run with balanced accuracy >= 0.64 and >= 90 % feasible completion; seeds of the same config span 0.59/0.48/0.71 stalled completion (analyst, unverified).

LEAKY CONTROL-FINGERPRINT CUE (verifier re-ran the model on the GPU with a sigma sweep and a second noise seed; the analyst's jittered numbers reproduce). What stall training added to wp8_p6_k80_prog is carried largely by the constancy of the recorded throttle while stuck (per-step |d throttle| 0.015 stuck vs 0.031-0.037 moving at the same level 0.37-0.49): zero-mean per-step throttle noise removes it in proportion to its size - f105 launch failures held under 1 m/s from rest 68 % (analyze_v2_f105.txt: rest+rec >1 m/s 0.32) -> 51 % / 25 % / 7 % at sigma 0.01/0.02/0.03 (second seed 10 %); true-stop prediction (verifier's convention) 0.47 -> 0.33/0.18/0.09; in-stall hold 0.54 -> 0.50/0.25/0.17; a tracker-magnitude AR(1) perturbation (|d| 0.025/step) still gives 19 % / 0.16; wp8b_k120_p9 collapses likewise (0.56 -> 0.00 true stops); wp8_p3_k80 loses 47-62 %; the frozen model stays at 0.41-0.43 launch and 0.22-0.24 hold at every sigma (a floor effect). Constant throttle at the feasible launches' own mean level (0.44) makes the primary hold 49 % of FEASIBLE launches under 1 m/s at 3 s (frozen 3 %). Feeding the imagined tracker's own actions open loop removes about half of the launch-failure reproduction (68 % -> 30 %) and smoothing them restores only a quarter of that gap (-> 40 %). The model is not state-blind: under the jitter it still separates launch-failure rest states from feasible ones by 1.34 m/s at 3 s (frozen 1.31), so training kept the frozen model's state-based discrimination and added the control cue on top (healthy-load probe +0.22 m/s vs frozen +1.09). rollout_loss in scripts/traverse_wp2_train_map.py feeds recorded actions clean (context_noise perturbs z1_hist only). Unverified analyst detail: in closed loop 0 % of f105 launch failures stay below 0.5 m/s over 30 s for every model (median first move 0.9 s for the primary) and the primary launches them MORE readily than the frozen model (78 % vs 60 % exceed 1 m/s within 5 s); its lower completion comes from stalling later on the route.

TRAINING-ARENA REPRODUCTION IS ROUTE MEMORISATION, AND THE WRONG-MAP PROBE WAS NOT A TEST (mechanism verified here; closed-loop numbers analyst-reported). scripts/traverse_wp7_stall_diagnosis.py's wrong-map probe does torch.roll(env.env_maps, 1) over an episode list built in manifest order; because the list is grouped by layout, 78 % (f104, 243 envs) / 82 % (f105, 297 envs) of the envs receive the SAME layout's map (recomputed here with HEAD's classify), so the §12.2 statement that swapping the map changes the prediction by < 0.05 m/s was untested. With a corrected permutation (every env gets another layout's map) the primary's closed-loop completion on f104 is launch 0.11 -> 0.11, stop 0.31 -> 0.27, feasible 0.87 -> 0.85, and on f105 0.59 -> 0.56, 0.59 -> 0.61, 0.92 -> 0.87 (per-episode agreement 0.78-0.86); healthy tire loads raise the frozen model's launch completion 0.75 -> 0.90 (f104 0.64 -> 1.00) but the primary's 0.59 -> 0.56. Mean over the 40 runs, launch/stop/feasible closed-loop completion: f104 0.12 / 0.23 / 0.89 vs f105 0.59 / 0.67 / 0.90 - the from-rest reproduction works on training routes without reading the terrain, and only generic pessimism transfers. f104 stop prediction from context is saturated at Chrono's own rate: p 0/0.3/0.6/0.9 at K80 give 0.67/0.77/0.74/0.74 against a recorded signed-<0.5 rate of 0.74 (leaderboard f104_S_pre_stop; the K>=40 vs K=8 split 0.65-0.78 vs 0.47-0.54 is horizon, not event share).

(1) Pre-audit 'stop' class: stuck_from_displacement returned (n-40, 40) for a vehicle still moving over its final 2 s, so 'crawl' never fired (0 of 846) and every launched timeout that progressed >= 2 m was a 'stop' pinned at n-40 when still moving (134 of the 176 timeout 'stops' in wp7_cache_v1; 161/176 have mean |vx| > 0.5 over the 'stuck' tail). At the scored frame Chrono itself had |vx| < 0.5 in 45/102 f105 'stops' (22/23 stall-aborts, 23/79 timeouts) and 44/78 f104 (the notes' 40/102 uses a different frame convention); 62 of the 102 f105 reference frames lie beyond the recording. The committed analyze numbers (0.25/0.46 stop, 0.39/0.74 hold, 0.38/0.78 launch) reproduce and mix true and false stops (primary f105 0.46 = 30/45 where Chrono stopped + 17/57 where it was moving). Fixed: HEAD's events.json has 146 stops (104 stall + 42 timeout) + 134 crawls in wp7_cache_v1 (recomputed here); corrected true-stop rates (analyze_v2_f105.txt, n=46, |vx|) frozen 0.24 / primary 0.39 / p9 0.50, hold 0.22 / 0.54 / 0.61, launch held 0.20 / 0.55 / 0.39, false stops 0.03 / 0.01 / 0.00. (2) stall_score's 'approach' term scores |pred vx| against zero where the recorded speed at frame stop+39 averaged |vx| 1.22 m/s (signed mean 0.684 = logged stall_approach_rec; 56 % >= 0.5) - mostly the stop-class defect, but under the corrected class the recorded |vx| there still averages 0.59 with 37 % >= 0.5. (3) The 'stuck' training kind is nearly empty at long horizons: recomputed here from the training-time events.json, windows with context + K frames after the stop exist in 62/22/9/4 training episodes at K = 40/80/120/160 (median tail after the stop 40 frames because Chrono aborts 3 s into a stall), yet the kind takes 1/5 of the event share (12 % of every batch at p = 0.6). (4) 'recovery' is mostly a launch metric: first resume frame <= 70 in 110 of 133 training episodes (108 exactly at frame 40, the first frame the detector can fire) and 61 of 69 on f105 (recomputed here); genuine en-route recoveries 24 train / 9 val. (5) Over-holding: seeded inside a stall the primary holds 34/42 windows where Chrono was stationary but also 41/60 where Chrono moved on (agreement 0.52 vs frozen 0.67). (6) Reporting: traverse_wp8_leaderboard.py's regex 'in-stall \+4s ([\d.]+)' has no sign, so f104_S_hold is blank for 34 of 40 wp8 rows (my count; e.g. wp8_p6_k80_prog 'in-stall +4s -0.12 (<0.5: 0.87)') - exactly the runs that hold best. (7) No validation-arena leakage into training; the harness is deterministic (re-runs reproduce every committed number; the primary's f105 imagination reproduces 161 rejects, 102/59, regret 1.17 from ckpt_best.pt); the 60 deg termination and tracker action centre were applied uniformly within wp8 (the action-centre change only affects the two scratch runs, whose act_mean differs from the frozen normaliser).
refuted_or_corrected: Notes 13.4 'Only three axes move the validation stall metrics beyond noise ... -0.29 m/s from p 0 to 0.6' -> five axes (lr 1e-4 and dropout are beyond noise in the same OLS, t = 2.5 and 4.0); the p and K effects are thresholds (step at p > 0 of ~-0.19, saturating by 0.3; step between K 40 and 80), and the OLS's -0.29 is about twice the directly observed matched-pair mean (-0.15) because the main-effects fit credits the progress-loss gain of the p >= 0.6, K >= 80 runs to p. 'Progress helps at K 80 but not K 40' is not identified (the two points differ in p as well). 'Data mix and the combined configuration inside the noise' is wrong: mix is -0.22 at (p.3,K40,prog) and the combo runs are +0.09 to +0.16 above the primary's seeds. 'Residual sd 0.12' is lack of fit (0.055 under the step model), not replicate noise (~0.03).

Axes claim 'best-checkpoint stall_score reproducible to ~0.02 across seeds' -> holds for one family only (0.015 spread); the combo pair differs by 0.067; pooled seed sd ~0.028, pairwise floor ~0.08, 13 of 40 runs inside it. Same-step spread '~0.09' mixes converged (0.02-0.06 at steps 2000-6000) and unconverged/drifting checkpoints (0.12-0.16 at 1000 and 8000-10000).

Notes 13.5 / pick claim 'The gap between own pick and gate+fastest is entirely in the cost ranking, not the gate; every own-pick failure is a slow candidate that stalls or times out' -> refuted as universal: 1-2 losses per model are all-rejected layouts won only by the fallback (without the fallback: 43/50, 46/51, 43/50, 44/48, 45/50), the gate falsely accepts the fastest candidate on 0-2 layouts where the own pick is feasible, contacts are 2-4 of each model's own-pick failures (some at 4.8-5.7 m/s, e.g. x_hill3_h270 direct_v8), and the 'oracle ranking on the accepted set = 50/50' counterfactual is nearly vacuous because accept-everything + oracle also gives 52/52.

Notes 13.5 'the imagined energy gradient (slow = cheap) outweighs the imagined time penalty' -> true only for the frozen model (energy under-predicted by -106 kJ at v2-3 vs -19 at v7-9; slower cheaper in 63 % of within-layout pairs). For the fine-tuned models the imagined cost is as speed-neutral as Chrono's (primary: slower route cheaper in 46 % of accepted pairs vs Chrono 47 %; p9 35 % with slow = MORE energy) and they OVER-predict energy on feasible routes, most at slow speeds (primary +62 kJ at v2-3 vs +43 at v7-9; p9 +133 vs +64). The slow drag comes from a minority of layouts (primary 12) where a slow rough climb's energy and time are badly under-imagined (x_hill0_h135 direct_v2: 78 kJ imagined vs 248 kJ + stall; on those layouts imagined slow-fast = time +1.9 + E/10 -17.8 vs Chrono +8.6 + 15.7), so the cost transmits an imagination error rather than mis-weighting a correct trade-off. Also 'gate+fastest averages 5.0 m/s' is the wrong yardstick: the Chrono-optimal pick averages 4.11 m/s. 'Time alone recovers most of the gap' fails for p9_k80_prog (43 -> 42) and wp8b_k120_p9 (41 -> 40).

Notes 13.4 'imagining feasible routes 1.6 s / 6.9 s slower than Chrono' -> recomputed here: the mean over all 451 feasible routes is +1.61 / +6.90 s only because rejected feasible routes sit at the 30 s imagined timeout; on accepted feasible routes the imagined time is unbiased (frozen -0.36 s, primary -0.19 s, k120_p9 +0.20 s; median img/Chrono ratio 0.98 for all three).

Notes 13.5 'P(max >= 47) = 0.51' -> 0.49 (exact Poisson-binomial and 200k-draw Monte Carlo; immaterial). Method claim 'the true per-run gate effect is about +0.8 layout' -> unsupported: the +0.78 is the in-sample f105 mean, comes almost entirely from one contact layout (18/40 runs) and one detour layout (9/40; +0.5 without detour eligibility), is matched by the plain fine-tune (+1) and the frozen model (0), and the five sealed runs average 0.0 vs the heuristic where +0.8/52 would predict about +1.4 on 93 layouts; the evidence supports a gate effect indistinguishable from zero on unseen arenas.

Method claim 'gate >= heuristic is close to guaranteed regardless of model quality' -> overreach: a matched-rate random rejecter scores 43.9 +/- 0.7 and falls BELOW the heuristic in ~20 % of draws (at rejection rates 0.7/0.9: 43-63 %), an anti-discriminating rejecter scores 15/52, and the models' 39/40 >= 44 and 27/40 > 44 exceed the random rates - i.e. the metric is heavily compressed (fallback +1.6, second-fastest feasible 42/44, only 8 fixable layouts), not one-sidedly protected. Two evidence numbers were wrong: own-pick abstention on the 13 no-solution layouts is 0-7 per run (not 0-2), and reject-AUC over the 40 runs on f105 is 0.53-0.70 (0.62-0.71 holds only for the 5 sealed-evaluated runs).

Closed-loop claim 'the tracker-in-the-loop pre-stop test is the only local number that predicts the closed-loop outcome well' -> it predicts only the local rest+tracker completion on the same 102 stop routes (-0.83), is itself pessimism-laden (-0.71 with feasible completion; the same test on feasible routes predicts stop completion at -0.74), adds nothing for launch failures, and like every f105 local number it does not predict the planner's pick (r = +0.02). '2-3x improvement' is per-metric best-of-40 (2.0-2.2x; ~1.5x for the average run). The teacher-forced tests are not devoid of discrimination signal (Youden J +0.45 / +0.51).

Closed-loop jitter claim: 'sigma 0.03, the size of the tracker's own closed-loop variability' -> the white jitter is ~1.6x the imagined tracker's per-step change (0.041 vs 0.026) with the opposite autocorrelation (-0.19 vs +0.28) and inflates feasible-run speed too (3.32 -> 3.71 m/s at 3 s vs Chrono 3.15); a tracker-matched AR(1) perturbation removes about two thirds rather than 70-90 %. 'Not on the physical state' -> refuted: state-based discrimination survives the jitter at the frozen level (1.34 vs 1.31 m/s). 'Smoothing the feasible controls makes the primary predict false stops on 11 %/16 %' -> came from a mis-indexed test (controls taken from the episode start, mean throttle 0.444 instead of 0.288); correctly indexed, 0 %/3 % below 0.5 m/s. '70-90 %' holds for two runs (p3_k80 loses 47-62 %); 'frozen unaffected' is a floor effect (moves +0.11 m/s in the same direction); the quoted stop baselines (0.49/0.77/0.78/0.86) are the pre-audit stop class with signed speed.

Audit stop-class claim: '|vx| < 0.5 in only 40/102 f105 stops and 37/78 f104' -> under the harness's own frame convention (t_stop + 40 clipped to the last recorded frame) 45/102 and 44/78; the split of the primary's 0.46 moves by ~5 episodes (30/45 + 17/57, not 29/40 + 18/62); 'every timeout that moved >= 2 m becomes a stop at frame n-40' -> every such timeout became a 'stop', but only those still moving in the final 2 s were pinned at n-40 (134 of 176). Notes 13.6 item 1 quotes the analyst's 40/102. The defect is already fixed at HEAD 34b5060.

what_the_summary_missed: The throttle-constancy cue. Notes 13.7-13.8 locate the closed-loop gap in 'the controller-model pairing' and rule out a throttle bias by shifting the throttle LEVEL (+/-0.2 leaves AUC 0.85-0.89); nobody varied the throttle's step-to-step VARIABILITY. The jitter probe shows the stall-trained models read the Chrono tracker's held-constant throttle (|d| 0.015/step stuck vs 0.031-0.037 moving) as the stall marker: sigma 0.03 per-step noise takes the primary's launch-failure hold from 68 % to 7 % and true-stop prediction from 0.47 to 0.09 while the frozen model sits at its floor; constant throttle at 0.44 stalls 49 % of FEASIBLE launches. The tracker never produces that signature (its imagined per-step change is 0.026 with positive autocorrelation), which explains why teacher-forced discrimination (AUC 0.89) does not survive the tracker (0.71) and why the trainer's clean recorded actions (rollout_loss perturbs only z1_hist) let the cue in. This bears directly on 13.8 step 2: a tracker retrained inside this imagination may learn to escape imagined stalls by dithering its throttle (an exploit of the cue) rather than by driving better - that step should not be launched until the cue is closed off.

The §12.2 wrong-map probe never swapped maps for most envs (roll-by-one over a layout-grouped list: 78 % f104 / 82 % f105 same-layout maps, recomputed here), so 'not the map' was asserted without a test; the corrected permutation happens to give the same closed-loop answer. Together with the healthy-load and wrong-map results on f104 (launch completion 0.11 -> 0.11 in both), the training-arena 'reproduce known examples' check passed by route memorisation: the f104 reproduction is horizon-driven and saturated at Chrono's own rate (0.67-0.77 vs recorded 0.74), and none of it depends on the scene map.

The 'stuck' training kind is almost empty at the horizons used because Chrono aborts 3 s into a stall (median tail 40 frames): 62/22/9/4 training episodes supply the windows at K 40/80/120/160 (recomputed here), yet the kind draws 12-18 % of every batch; 'recovery' windows are 108/133 launches-from-rest at frame 40. The ablation therefore never trained 'stall persistence over 2-4 s' on more than a couple of dozen episodes, and the K >= 120 runs on 4-9.

Threshold structure and interactions the linear OLS hid: p saturates at 0.3 (going to 0.6/0.9 only adds rejected feasible routes), K matters only as a 2 s -> 4 s step, progress loss flips sign between the two grid points, the combo is worse than its parent because of dropout, and the data mix helps at (p.3,K40,prog) by -0.22. wp8_p6_k120_prog diverged at step 4000 (val_loss 0.105 -> 1.06), so the K = 120 axis conclusion rests on a 2000-step checkpoint; 14 of 40 runs' selected checkpoints are 1000 steps of fine-tuning.

The selection double-dip: checkpoints are chosen by stall_score on f105 windows and every reported f105 stall test and pick uses f105 (and the pick-gate 'best run' was then chosen by the f105 maximum). The unbiased readouts are f104 (for reproduction) and the sealed set; f105 seed spreads are understated.

The f105 'stall-route acceptance' did not move at all for the primary (31/36 accepted, same as the frozen model); what the imagination learned is to time out slow routes (timeouts accepted 63/63 -> 39/63) and, as a side effect, to reject 59-199 feasible routes. On accepted feasible routes the imagined time is unbiased (median ratio 0.98) - the '1.6 s / 6.9 s slower' in 13.4 is an artefact of averaging over imagined timeouts. A second all-feasible layout, s_hill4_crater7_t+60_sh (correct pose, 9/9 Chrono-feasible), is rejected 7-9/9 by the p >= 0.6 models as 800+ kJ imagined timeouts and 0/9 by the frozen model - a specific imagination failure worth its own look, distinct from the heading-flip layout.

The gate+fastest 'fixes' are dominated by a contact failure rejected for an unrelated imagined timeout (18/40 runs) and a detour candidate (9/40); the plain earlier fine-tune wp7_ft_mix_amd scores 45, the same as the median ablation run, so the whole 40-run sweep did not move the gate metric relative to a plain fine-tune; the fallback alone is worth +1.6 layouts and a random rejecter lands at 43.9 +/- 0.7. No f105 local metric - not the stall score, not the corrected stall tests, not even closed-loop stop completion - correlates with either pick endpoint (|r| <= 0.2).

The cost ranking is nearly speed-neutral in Chrono (the faster of two feasible same-layout routes is cheaper in 53 % of pairs; the Chrono-optimal pick averages 4.1 m/s) and, for the fine-tuned models, in imagination too; the own pick loses because a minority of slow rough climbs are imagined far too easy (78 vs 248 kJ), not because of the energy weight. Ranking accepted routes by imagined time recovers 74 % of the own-to-gate gap but only by becoming 'fastest accepted'.

Analyst observations not adversarially verified but consistent with the files: in closed loop the primary launches launch failures more readily than the frozen model (78 % vs 60 % exceed 1 m/s within 5 s) and its extra non-completions are later time-outs (84 time-outs vs 1 attitude failure), so the closed-loop 'reproduction' is generic pessimism along the route; the from-scratch runs have the lowest val_loss (0.064 vs 0.10) and z1_mae_norm@100 (0.54 vs 0.74) with the worst stall metrics (1.32/1.67), so the z1_100 column is not comparable across the init axis without checking the normaliser; the pre-audit 'stops' were mostly the last 2 s of a 16 s struggle (first station reached at median 7.5 s, first below 1 m/s at 6.0 s, minimum vx median -2.2 m/s) - the crawl fix removes the moving ones, but the 'approach' windows still end 2 s before a stop frame that sits well after the loss of momentum the planner has to foresee.
synthesis.recommendation: Do not run a sealed confirmation now: the sealed arenas are spent (three looks; heuristic fails on 7/93, ceiling +4, five gated runs average 0.0 vs the heuristic), and no run has shown closed-loop discrimination that would survive one. Before 13.8 step 2 (retraining the tracker inside the stall-aware imagination, cluster time), settle the throttle-constancy cue with one local, pre-registered experiment, because a tracker trained inside an imagination whose stall signal is 'throttle held constant' can learn to dither its way out of imagined stalls. Pre-registration text: (1) Prerequisites (no training): regenerate events with the corrected stop class, the approach target changed to |pred-rec| like 'matched', resume events at frame <= 40 excluded from 'recovery', and the stuck kind's share reduced to its episode count; add two probes to the analyze harness - per-step throttle perturbation matched to the imagined tracker (AR(1), |d throttle| 0.025/step, lag-1 autocorrelation +0.3; also white sigma 0.03 for comparison) on the rest, pre-stop and in-stall tests, and a wrong-map permutation that assigns every env a different layout's map; fix the leaderboard regex. Score the existing wp8_p6_k80_prog, its two seeds, wp8_p3_k80, wp8b_k120_p9 and the frozen model with these probes on f104, f105 and the corrected true-stop semantics (analyze_v2), reporting per-episode agreement with Chrono plus |pred-rec|. (2) One training run on the cluster: wp8_p6_k80_prog's configuration (p 0.6, K 80, progress 1, lr 3e-4, fine-tune from the frozen model, seed 20260903) with action-input augmentation in rollout_loss and step_loss - per-step AR(1) throttle/steer noise of the tracker's magnitude plus random 0.5 s smoothing, applied to the actions the model conditions on, never to the targets - selected by the corrected stall_score at the checkpoint rule 'lowest corrected score at step <= 5000', evaluated with the identical harness. (3) Primary endpoints, fixed in advance, on f105 true stops (n 46) and launch failures (n 105) with |vx| < 0.5: (a) the augmented model's un-jittered true-stop prediction, in-stall hold and launch hold must be >= 0.30 / 0.45 / 0.45 (frozen 0.24 / 0.22 / 0.20; primary 0.39 / 0.54 / 0.55) AND must fall by < 0.10 under the AR(1) probe (the primary falls from 0.47 to 0.16 and 68 % to 19 % under the verifier's convention); (b) the 13.7 decision test with the tracker in the loop must reach AUC >= 0.80 for 'stuck within 8 s' (primary 0.71 tracker vs 0.89 recorded controls; frozen 0.76) with feasible-route closed-loop completion >= 0.90 (primary 0.92). (4) Decision rule: if (a) and (b) hold, the cue was the fingerprint, closed-loop discrimination is attainable from the state, and 13.8 step 2 (tracker inside the augmented imagination) proceeds, followed by fresh sealed arenas f108+ generated model-free with >= 30 layouts on which the fastest heuristic fails but a feasible alternative exists, one look, paired sign test at fix:break >= 3:1 and p <= 0.05, checkpoint chosen by the seed-median rule, contact-only and no-solution layouts reported apart. If (a) fails (the stall metrics collapse to the frozen level once the cue is removed), the ablation's stall reproduction was the fingerprint; stop training this loss on these events and go to the terrain-reading problem (the s_hill4_crater7_t+60_sh and x_hill1_h180 failures, the stall/progress head, or the replanning design) instead. If (a) holds but (b) fails, the gap is genuinely the controller pairing and step 2 proceeds with the augmented model. One run, one look at f105, analysis script committed before the run finishes.

surprises: The leaderboard's f104_S_hold column is blank for 33 runs because traverse_wp8_leaderboard.py's regex `in-stall \+4s ([\d.]+)` does not match negative predicted speeds (e.g. wp8_p6_k80_prog: 'in-stall +4s -0.12 (<0.5: 0.87)'); the values exist in analyze_f104.txt (0.56-0.90) and are missing exactly for the runs that hold stalls best.

Progress loss has opposite signs at the two grid points (-0.22 at p.6/K80, +0.21 at p.3/K40), so the 'progress loss helps' conclusion rests on one pair; its clearest effect is on the guard terms (v_recov -0.32, v_match -0.30, 10x the seed sd of 0.03), i.e. it makes the model track recorded motion better rather than predict more stops.

Lower learning rate (1e-4) and dropout both make stall metrics worse (+0.23 and +0.20 per 0.1), and the regularised 'combo' (0.91/0.84) is worse than its unregularised parent k120_prog (0.79): regularisation does not fix the overfitting, it just starts the fine-tune from a damaged pretrained model (val_loss 0.121-0.133 at step 1000 vs 0.102).

The stall_score that ranks the runs is 43% driven by the two guard terms (matched/recovery |pred-rec|); the hold fractions it is meant to capture top out at v_appr 0.39 and v_launch 0.50 even in the best runs, and v_stuck is computed from 17 windows.

Checkpoint selection (min stall_score over 5-14 evaluations on f105) and all reported f105 tests/picks use the same arena, so the f105 numbers are optimistically selected and the seed spread on them is understated; f104 and the sealed arenas are the unbiased readouts.

wp8_p6_k120_prog blew up at step 4000 (val_loss 0.105 -> 1.11), a training-stability failure at K=120 with lr 3e-4 that did not recur in wp8b_k120_p9, wp8b_k160 or the combo runs; its leaderboard entry is the pre-divergence step-2000 checkpoint.

From-scratch runs have far lower val_loss (0.064 vs 0.10) and z1_mae_norm@100 (0.54 vs 0.74) than every fine-tuned run yet the worst stall metrics (1.32/1.67); either the normalisation statistics differ between scratch and init-from runs (making these columns incomparable) or the standard error metrics are anti-correlated with stall behaviour, and the leaderboard's z1_100 column should not be used across the init axis without checking.
result.next_step: Close the open-loop/closed-loop gap before touching training again: for wp8_p6_k80_prog and the frozen model, re-run the imagination on the 37 f105 stall routes with the recorded controls instead of the tracker (the 'model' subcommand of traverse_wp7_stall_diagnosis.py already does the open-loop part) and tabulate per-route img_ok under both control sources. The open-loop tests say the fine-tuned model holds 74% of stalls and predicts 46-78% of stops, yet tracker-driven imagination still accepts 86% of stall routes; if recorded-control imagination rejects them, the bottleneck is the tracker adapting throttle inside the imagination (and a stall/progress head or a tracker-aware acceptance rule is the fix), not any of the training axes, whose pick effects are all inside the 3-layout noise.

findings.claim: Rejecting the fastest candidate is wrong two thirds of the time but almost never costs the gate+fastest pick, because the next-fastest accepted route is feasible; the gains over the heuristic come mostly from one CONTACT failure rejected for the wrong reason, and the stall-only ceiling on f105 is 48/52.
findings.evidence: /tmp/wp8lens/fastrej.py over all 42 evaluated models: fastest candidate rejected 290 times; 189 wrongly (fastest feasible) with a feasible fallback in 187 (99 %; the 2 breaks are wp8b_combo and wp8_p6_k8 on x_hill1_h000_sh); 101 rightly, but the fallback was feasible in only 34 (34 %) because on the hill3 layouts every direct candidate fails and the models accept the slower direct ones too. The heuristic's 8 failures: 4 contact (s_hill3_hill1_t-60_sh seq_v8_8, x_hill3_h000/h045/h270 direct_v8/v9), 2 stall (f_04 free_5_v9, x_hill1_h000 direct_v8), 2 timeout (x_hill3_h180/h225 direct_v8). Fix counts over 42 models: s_hill3_hill1_t-60_sh 18 (Chrono contact; models reject seq_v8_8 by imagined timeout while also rejecting 6-7 of the 8 feasible routes on that layout), x_hill3_h180 9, x_hill3_h270 3 (contact), f_04 3, x_hill3_h225 1. wp8_p6_k80_prog's +3 = f_04 (rejects free_5_v9 and free_0_v3/free_3_v5 too, accepts free_1_v4 stall + free_2_v5 feasible), s_hill3_hill1_t-60_sh (contact), x_hill3_h180 (rejects direct_v4-v9, accepts direct_v2/v3 which also time out, plus detour_R). x_hill1_h000 (11/13 fail, perched launch) is accepted at every speed by every model.

findings.claim: Even with a perfect feasibility gate the imagined cost ranking is worse than 'fastest', and across the 40 ablation runs the own-pick count is noise unrelated to the stall metrics, while gate+fastest is the heuristic +/- 2.
findings.evidence: /tmp/wp8lens/perfectgate.py: ranking only Chrono-feasible routes by imagined cost gives regret 1.23 (frozen), 1.19 (p6), 1.18 (p9), 1.21 (p3_k80), 1.20 (match3ap2) vs 1.15 for perfect gate + fastest and 1.11 for perfect gate + Chrono time; pairwise agreement of imagined vs Chrono cost order among accepted feasible routes 0.68-0.71 (vs 0.54 for 'faster is cheaper'). /tmp/wp8lens/corr.py over 40 wp8 runs: own-pick feasible 31-43 (mean 38.8), Spearman rho with stall_score -0.07, rej_inf -0.06, rej_feas -0.08, f105_S_trk_done 0.00; gate+fastest 43-46 (mean 44.5), rho with rej_feas -0.41. Frozen own pick 39 with 29 rejections; fine-tuned 41-43 with 95-123 rejections.

surprises: The quoted gate+fastest numbers (47/46/46/46/44) are reproduced only when the slope_aware profile is eligible as 'fastest accepted' and candidates are ranked by recorded mean_speed; with the same candidate set the pick table's fastest heuristic uses (commanded-speed candidates only) the numbers are 46 (p6_k80_prog), 44 (p3_k80, no gain), 45 (p6_k120_prog), 45 (match3ap2), 44 (frozen) (/tmp/wp8lens/gatevariants.py).

The heading-flip layout x_hill1_h180 costs every model 13 false rejections and one own pick (nothing accepted): the leaderboard's rej_feas column is inflated by 13 for every run (the frozen model's 23 is really 10), and the own-pick totals by 1.

Most of gate+fastest's advantage over the heuristic on f105 is a contact failure (s_hill3_hill1_t-60_sh) rejected by an imagined timeout while 6-7 of the 8 feasible routes on the same layout are rejected too -- coincidence, not stall reproduction; genuine stall/timeout fixes are x_hill3_h180 (9 of 42 models), f_04 (3), x_hill3_h225 (1).

The fine-tuned models overestimate energy on feasible routes by 18-82 % (worst at slow speeds), yet still rank slow candidates cheapest because the imagined energy gradient with speed exceeds the time penalty at weight 1/10; the frozen model instead underestimates slow-route energy by 44 %. Both errors push the same way.

s_hill4_crater7_t+60_sh is a second all-feasible layout that the fine-tuned imagination fails wholesale (7-9 of 9 routes imagined as timeouts, 800+ kJ) with a correct start pose -- a genuine imagination failure worth its own look, distinct from the heading flip.
result.next_step: Pre-register and run one selection-rule change on the sealed arenas (imagine_sealed/rows.json already exists for 5 runs): keep wp8_p6_k80_prog only as a rejecter and rank accepted candidates by commanded speed (or imagined time with energy weight <= 0.02), with the fastest-overall fallback, excluding or fixing the heading-flipped layout; compare against the fastest heuristic on the 93 sealed layouts. This tests directly whether the +2-3 f105 gain (which on f105 is 1 stall + 1 timeout + 1 contact coincidence) survives, before spending more on stall reproduction in the model itself.

findings.claim: The local (teacher-forced) stall tests improved 2-3x but track the runs' overall pessimism, not their ability to tell stalled from feasible routes; the tracker-in-the-loop pre-stop test is the only local number that predicts the closed-loop outcome well.
findings.evidence: Parsed all 42 analyze_f105.txt (/tmp/wp8lens/parse.py, corr.py). Frozen -> best runs: stop pre-stop reproduction 0.25 -> 0.55 (wp8_p6_k80_prog_s1), in-stall hold 0.39 -> 0.78 (wp8b_k120_p9), launch in-context 0.38 -> 0.78 (wp8_p6_k80_prog). Across the 40 wp8 runs (Pearson): S_pre_rec<0.5 vs stop rest+trk done -0.59, vs feasible rest+trk done -0.66; L_pre_rec<0.5 vs launch done -0.53, vs feasible done -0.57; in-stall hold vs stop done -0.41. Stalled-run completion and feasible completion move together (r=+0.81, fit stall_done = 1.54*F_done - 0.76); correlation of the local tests with the residual of that fit (discrimination beyond pessimism) is -0.21 (L_pre), -0.09 (S_pre), -0.08 (hold). The pre-stop context + tracker test (S_pretrk) correlates -0.83 with stop closed-loop completion, +0.72 with separation (F_done - stall_done) and -0.46 with the residual.

findings.claim: The trained models' stall reproduction rests on a leaky cue in the recorded controls (the Chrono controller's near-constant throttle while stalled), not on the physical state or the terrain: a zero-mean throttle jitter of sigma 0.03 per step, the size of the tracker's own closed-loop variability, removes 70-90% of the reproduced stalls, while the frozen model is unaffected.
findings.evidence: Patched copy of the diagnosis script (/tmp/wp8lens/diag_patched.py, outputs /tmp/wp8lens/diag/raw_jit_*.npz, raw_jit2_*.npz, NaN-dropped semantics as in analyze). wp8_p6_k80_prog on f105: launch from rest + recorded controls vx@3s 0.66 (68% <1 m/s) -> 2.37 (7%) with throttle jitter; stop pre-stop <0.5: 0.49 -> 0.10; in-stall hold 0.77 -> 0.13; launch in-context 0.78 -> 0.09; in-stall hold (launch) 0.86 -> 0.05. wp8b_k120_p9: 0.56 -> 0.05, hold 0.83 -> 0.10. Frozen wp2_mapv2_pt_dag_ro8_amd: 0.26 -> 0.23, hold 0.41 -> 0.42. Steering jitter (2x sigma) barely matters (0.66 -> 0.77 m/s). Conversely smoothing the FEASIBLE controls (0.5 s moving average, level preserved) makes wp8_p6_k80_prog predict false stops on 11% of feasible controls (k120_p9 16%, frozen 0%), and a constant 0.44 throttle stalls 49% of feasible controls at 3 s (frozen 3%). Recorded step-to-step |d throttle| during launch failures is 0.008-0.019 vs the imagined tracker's 0.024-0.037 (raw6/raw2 outputs). The trainer feeds recorded actions clean (rollout_loss in scripts/traverse_wp2_train_map.py: context_noise perturbs z1_hist only), so nothing counteracts this.

findings.claim: In closed loop the tracker never supplies that cue, so the imagined vehicle launches every launch failure within about a second and the 'reproduced' stalls happen later along the route; the closed-loop gap for launch failures is entirely in the throttle/brake channel, and the from-rest open-loop hold is not even predictive per episode.
findings.evidence: raw1/raw2/mix experiments (/tmp/wp8lens/diag/raw_lens_*.npz, raw_mix_*.npz), f105 launch class n=105: under the tracker 0% of launch failures stay below 0.5 m/s over 30 s for every model (median first move 0.9 s for wp8_p6_k80_prog), 78% exceed 1 m/s within 5 s (frozen 60%); non-completed launch failures end at median 3.5 m progress, only 42% under 2 m (frozen: 0.8 m, 77%). Replaying the tracker's actions open-loop reproduces the closed loop exactly (|dvx| 0.000); recorded steer + tracker throttle/brake gives vx@3s 1.83 (36% <1) vs tracker steer + recorded throttle 0.80 (57% <1) vs all-recorded 0.66 (68%); smoothing the tracker's actions halves the effect (1.02, 48%). Scaling the recorded throttle x1.15 or +0.05 does nothing (0.77 / 0.69 m/s). Per episode, wp8_p6_k80_prog completes 59% of the launch failures it held under recorded controls and 59% of those it did not (frozen 47% vs 97%); for stops, 52% of the reproduced vs 65% of the non-reproduced. The launch-class from-rest recorded-controls test did improve in step with the in-context test (r=-0.82 across runs; >1 m/s at 3 s: frozen 57% -> 32% wp8_p6_k80_prog, 31% wp8_p6_k120_prog), but it is the same jitter-fragile cue, and only 15% never move within 30 s.

findings.claim: The from-rest stall reproduction works on the training arena but not on the unseen arena, and neither depends on the scene map: the models memorised the training routes' state/control trajectories rather than learning to read the terrain, so on new terrain only generic pessimism remains.
findings.evidence: analyze_f104.txt vs analyze_f105.txt over the 40 runs (mean): launch rest+trk done 0.12 (f104) vs 0.59 (f105), stop 0.23 vs 0.67, feasible 0.89 vs 0.90; wp8_p6_k80_prog 0.11/0.31/0.87 vs 0.59/0.59/0.92; frozen 0.64/0.95/0.98 vs 0.75/0.92/0.98. Corrected wrong-map probe (every env gets another layout's map; /tmp/wp8lens/diag/raw_wm2_*.npz): closed-loop completion for wp8_p6_k80_prog f104 launch 0.11 -> 0.11, stop 0.31 -> 0.27, feasible 0.87 -> 0.85; f105 0.59 -> 0.56, 0.59 -> 0.61, 0.92 -> 0.87; per-episode agreement right vs wrong map 0.78-0.86. Healthy tire loads: closed-loop launch completion frozen 0.75 -> 0.90 (f104 0.64 -> 1.00) but wp8_p6_k80_prog 0.59 -> 0.56, i.e. training replaced the frozen model's weak physical cue (tire loads) with the control fingerprint. The imagined approach speed on f105 is not the problem any more: at 15/10/5 m before the recorded stop station the tracker-from-rest speed is 1.23/1.67/2.25 m/s (wp8_p6_k80_prog) vs Chrono 1.15/1.70/2.28 (frozen 1.23/1.73/2.42).

findings.claim: The runs that close the closed-loop gap most do so mainly by stalling more of everything; the best separation is wp8_p3_k80, the best pick-gate result wp8_p6_k80_prog, and seed noise is as large as the differences between configurations.
findings.evidence: tradeoff.py from analyze_f105.txt + imagine_f105/rows.json + pick_f105.json. Stalled-run completion (launch+stop weighted, n=207) / feasible-control completion (n=265): frozen 0.83/0.98; wp8_p3_k80 0.40/0.87 (separation 0.47, residual -0.18, rejects 81/451 feasible bank routes, gate 46/52); wp8b_k120_p9 0.19/0.62 (0.43, 199/451 rejected, gate 44/52); wp8_p6_k80_prog_mix 0.45/0.85 (0.40); wp8_p6_k80_prog 0.59/0.92 (0.33, 59/451, gate 47/52, the only run with balanced rejecter accuracy 0.64 and >=90% feasible completion); wp8b_noise20 0.81/0.94 (0.13, no better than frozen 0.15 despite in-context 0.70/0.75). Balanced accuracy as a rejecter (451 feasible/207 stalled f105 routes): frozen 0.55, wp8_p3_k80 0.71, wp8_p6_k80_prog_s1 0.70, wp8_p6_k80_prog 0.64. Seeds of the same config (wp8_p6_k80_prog, _s1, _s2): stalled completion 0.59/0.48/0.71, feasible 0.92/0.87/0.92. Gate-check feasible picks span 43-47 of 52 and correlate +0.21 with separation, -0.06 with stalled completion. Non-completions of stalled routes are almost all time-outs (imagined stalls), not attitude/cross-track failures (wp8_p6_k80_prog 84 time-outs vs 1 failure; exception wp8_p6_k8: 56 failures).

findings.claim: The 'stop' events that anchor the local tests and the event-balanced training are mostly the last two seconds of a 30 s timeout after a long back-and-forth struggle, so the tests measure holding a 15-second-old stall, not the loss of momentum the planner has to foresee.
findings.evidence: classify.json (arena_f105 stops, n=102) + recorded traces (raw4.py): stop_s = 28.0 s for 57 of 102 (79 have n_frames 600, status timeout; stuck tail exactly 2.0 s for 62); the vehicle first reaches the final station at median 7.5 s, first drops below 1 m/s at median 6.0 s, then struggles a median 16.4 s (mean vx during the struggle 0.06 m/s, minimum vx median -2.18 m/s, i.e. rolling back; slip-back median 1.5 m) before the detected stop; the pre-stop test starts at 26 s and the 'approach' training windows end 2 s before the same frame. On the training arenas 44% of the 178 stops also have stop_s = 28.0 (median 27.4 s).

surprises: The wrong-map probe in scripts/traverse_wp7_stall_diagnosis.py rolls env_maps by one, and because the episode list is grouped by layout, 79% (f104) / 83% (f105) of the envs receive the SAME layout's map; the notes' statement that swapping the map changes the prediction by <0.05 m/s was not a real test. A corrected probe (different layout for every env) gives the same answer for the closed loop, so the conclusion survives, but by luck.

The trained models' stall reproduction is a control-fingerprint effect: sigma 0.03 iid throttle jitter (smaller than the tracker's own closed-loop variability) collapses wp8_p6_k80_prog's local stall metrics from 0.49/0.77/0.78/0.86 to 0.10/0.13/0.09/0.05 while leaving the frozen model unchanged; the in-training stall_score and the analyze_f105 local columns are therefore measuring how well the model recognises the Chrono controller's reaction to a stall, not the stall.

On the training arena the closed-loop imagination reproduces the stalls from rest (launch 0.11, stop 0.31 for wp8_p6_k80_prog) even with another layout's scene map and even with healthy tire loads (0.29), so the 'reproduce known training examples' check passed through route memorisation, not terrain reading.

In closed loop the trained model launches launch failures MORE readily than the frozen one (78% vs 60% exceed 1 m/s within 5 s); its lower completion comes from stalling later on the route, not from reproducing the launch failure.

Chrono's 'stops' are mostly 16 s of rocking/rolling back followed by the 2 s timeout tail; the recorded approach speed near the stall point (1.15-2.28 m/s at 15-5 m before) is now matched by the trained imagination, so the remaining gap is not approach-speed optimism as notes 12.2 item 6 suggested.
result.next_step: Retrain one configuration (wp8_p6_k80_prog) with action-input augmentation in rollout_loss and step_loss (per-step Gaussian throttle/steer jitter matched to the imagined tracker's variability, sigma about 0.03, plus random 0.5 s smoothing), select the checkpoint by the tracker-in-the-loop pre-stop test instead of stall_score, and re-evaluate with the jitter probe added to the analyze table (pre+rec with jitter, in-stall hold with jitter) and the corrected wrong-map permutation; if the local stall metrics survive the jitter probe and f105 closed-loop stalled-run completion drops without a matching drop in feasible completion, the leaky-cue explanation is confirmed and the remaining gap is the terrain-reading problem, otherwise the ablation's gains were the fingerprint and further training of this loss is not worth cluster time.

findings.claim: The 'stop' class is mis-defined: `classify_episode` in scripts/traverse_wp7_stall_diagnosis.py sets `stuck_end = run * DT >= 2.0 or status == 'stall'`, but `stuck_from_displacement` can never return a run shorter than its 40-frame window, so `stuck_end` is always True, the 'crawl' class is unreachable (0 of 846 classified runs) and every timeout that moved >= 2 m becomes a 'stop' at frame n-40. Roughly half of the 'stops' the stall tests score against were still moving in Chrono at the reference frame, so the headline 'stops predicted' rates mix true stops with false stops.
findings.evidence: wp7_cache_v1 events.json: 280 'stop' episodes = 176 timeouts + 104 stall-aborts; 134 of the timeouts have stop == n-40 (the detector floor), 161 of 176 have mean |vx| > 0.5 m/s over the 'stuck' tail (e.g. arena_f105__f_00__free_3_v5: vx goes -2.98 -> +3.3 m/s across the 'stop', 2.6 m/s at the end). At the analyze 'pre+rec vx@+2s' frame Chrono has |vx| < 0.5 in only 40/102 f105 stops (91% of the 23 stall-aborts, 24% of the 79 timeouts) and 37/78 f104 stops. Re-running `model`/`analyze` for the frozen model and wp8_p6_k80_prog into /tmp/wp8_audit reproduces the committed analyze_f105/f104 numbers exactly (0.25/0.46 stop, 0.39/0.74 hold, 0.38/0.78 launch); per-episode: the primary's f105 0.46 = 29/40 stops where Chrono stopped + 18/62 where Chrono was still moving (agreement 0.72 vs frozen 0.54; |pred-rec| 0.69 vs 2.55 m/s); f104 0.74 = 34/37 + 24/41 (agreement 0.65 vs 0.46; |pred-rec| 0.36 vs 1.66 m/s).

findings.claim: The checkpoint-selection metric `stall_score` (scripts/traverse_wp2_train_map.py stall_eval) is mis-specified and then used on the same arena the leaderboard reports: its 'approach' term is mean |pred vx| with an implicit target of 0 although the recorded speed at the end of those 102 f105 windows averages |vx| 1.22 m/s (56% >= 0.5, 43% >= 1 m/s; logged stall_approach_rec = 0.684); the 'stuck' term has n = 17 (quantised at 1/17, with near-duplicate siblings such as x_hill3_h180 direct_v8/v9); and selection by this score on f105 windows is followed by reporting analyze_f105 / pick_f105 on f105.
findings.evidence: stall_eval specs: approach -> mode 'abs'; train_log val records: stall_approach_rec 0.684, stall_stuck_n 17, stall_approach_n 102; recomputed recorded vx at frame stop+39 on f105: mean|.| 1.22, frac |vx|<0.5 0.44, frac >1 0.33, frac <-1 0.10 (stall-aborts 0.96 stationary, timeouts 0.29). All 40 wp8 configs have selection='stall_score', val_arenas=['arena_f105']; ckpt_best steps match the best stall_score step for all 40 runs, 14 of 40 at step 1000 (the first evaluation); the three seeds of the best family score 0.75/0.76/0.77 and pick 40/40/41, i.e. most wave-2 differences are inside seed noise. The one clean test is the pre-registered sealed check in the uncommitted notes 13.5 (gate+fastest 85-87 vs heuristic 86; own picks 76-81 vs frozen 80), which is negative.

findings.claim: No run collapses to 'always stop' under the teacher-forced guards, but the stall-trained models over-hold in the stuck regime and are pessimistic in closed loop: seeded inside a 'stall', the primary keeps the vehicle stationary in most windows where Chrono actually moved on, and closed-loop completion of feasible routes drops from the frozen model's 0.98 to 0.62-0.96 across runs.
findings.evidence: Guards: v_match (|pred-rec| vx on matched feasible crossings, rec 3.26 m/s) 0.45-0.53 for the best family vs 0.73 (p0_k80) and 1.25 (p3_k8); f105 feasible teacher-forced false stops 0.00-0.05 (frozen 0.03). Over-holding (/tmp/wp8_audit re-run): in-stall probe on f105 stops, primary holds 34/42 windows where Chrono was stationary but also 41/60 where Chrono was moving (agreement 0.52 vs frozen 0.67); f104: 41/43 and 27/35 (0.63 vs 0.67). Closed loop, analyze_*: f105 feasible rest+trk done frozen 0.98, wp7_ft 0.97, primary family 0.87-0.92, wp8b_k120_p9 0.62, wp8b_combo_s1 0.74; f104 primary 0.87; sealed (analyze_sealed_wp8.txt) primary 0.84 vs frozen 0.99, and it rejects 113 feasible vs 68 infeasible bank routes (notes 13.5). The 'in-stall +4s' reference for windows past the end of the recording is the last 1 s of Chrono's trace, a proxy.

findings.claim: Requirement (1) 'reproduce known training examples' is only partly met: from the recorded context the primary reproduces the genuinely stationary training-arena stalls, but in closed loop from rest it still completes a third of the training-arena stops and fails 13% of the training-arena feasible controls, and the event-balanced sampling contributes little to the training-arena reproduction rate.
findings.evidence: analyze_f104 (training arena) for wp8_p6_k80_prog: stop pre+rec <0.5 = 0.74 (per-episode: 34/37 stall-aborts stopped, 14/14 stationary launch failures), in-stall hold 0.87, but rest+trk done = 0.31 for stops, 0.11 for launch failures (Chrono 0) and 0.87 for feasible controls (Chrono 1.0; frozen 0.98). f104 S_pre across event fractions at K=80: p=0 0.67, p=0.3 0.77, p=0.6 0.74, p=0.9 0.74 - the signed-<0.5 recorded rate at that frame is 0.74, so the metric is saturated at Chrono's own rate rather than measuring reproduction.

findings.claim: The data cannot support 'stall persistence over 2-4 s' as constructed: Chrono aborts 3 s into a stall (--stall-abort-s 3), so the 'stuck' event kind is nearly empty at the horizons used and the 'recovery' kind is dominated by ordinary launches from rest rather than recoveries from a stall.
findings.evidence: Recomputed MapBatcher.event_table (matches the notes' K=40 counts 7120/2764/2583/3694/26379 exactly): 'stuck' windows come from 62 training episodes at K=40, 22 at K=80 (1073 windows), 9 at K=120, 4 at K=160 (216 windows) - while receiving 1/5 of the event share (12% of every batch at p=0.6, 18% at p=0.9). Tail after the detected stop: median 40 frames on every arena. 'resume' events: 110 of 134 train and 61 of 70 val are at frame <= 70 (median exactly 40, the first frame the detector in cmd_events can fire; window covers frames 0-39, the 2 s launch window Chrono's own stall counter excludes); only 24 train / 9 val are en-route recoveries; the val stall_recovery windows are 38 feasible + 12 launch + 7 stop + 6 off_route + 3 contact + 3 stall_recovered episodes.

findings.claim: No leakage of the validation arena into training was found and the evaluation is deterministic; the remaining defects are reporting bugs: the leaderboard's in-stall regex fails on negative predicted speeds, blanking the f104/f105 'hold' cells for most of the better runs.
findings.evidence: traverse_wp2_train_map.py: MapBatcher.__init__ keeps only events of its own split's keys (`{k: events[k] for k in self.keys ...}`), splits are by arena (train f101-f104, val f105, test []), normaliser comes from the init checkpoint (fine-tunes) or Normalizer.fit(train_split) (scratch), 'matched' stations are keyed by arena-prefixed layout names. Re-running the stall tests for two checkpoints reproduced every committed analyze number. traverse_wp8_leaderboard.py: `re.search(r"in-stall \+4s ([\d.]+) \(<0.5: ([\d.]+)\)")` has no sign, so 35 of 40 runs (f104 in-stall vx negative, e.g. wp8_p6_k80_prog -0.12 (<0.5: 0.87)) show an empty f104_S_hold; the launch-class hold is not tabulated at all. Configs for wave 1 lack the 'context_noise' key (added in wave 2), harmless.

surprises: About half of the 'stop' events are not stops: the 'crawl' class can never fire (stuck_end is unconditionally True), so 176 timeouts - most of them vehicles rolling back or oscillating at 1-3 m/s on a slope - are scored as stationary stalls at frame n-40. Every headline 'stops predicted' / 'stall held' number in the leaderboard and in the uncommitted notes 13.4-13.6 inherits this.

The 'in-stall hold' improvement (frozen 0.39 -> primary 0.74 on f105) is mostly over-holding: per-episode agreement with Chrono is worse than the frozen model's (0.52 vs 0.67), because the primary holds 41 of the 60 windows in which Chrono moved on.

The 'recovery' guard is essentially a launch metric: the resume detector fires at frame 40 (the first frame it can) for any episode whose vehicle sat with throttle > 0.3 during the first 2 s; genuine en-route recoveries number 24 (train) and 9 (val).

The 'stuck' training kind at the main horizon K=80 is drawn from 22 episodes yet takes 12% of every batch (4 episodes at K=160), because Chrono's 3 s stall abort leaves a median 2 s tail after the detected stop.

The uncommitted notes already contain a pre-registered sealed check (13.5), and it is negative (gate changes the heuristic by -1 to +1 layout; own picks 76-81 below the frozen 80). The notes' statement that the reviewer's first two requirements 'are met' rests on the saturated fraction-<0.5 metric; on the training arena the models' 0.74-0.78 equals the recorded signed-<0.5 rate of 0.74.
The f105 'stops predicted' metric is signed (`vx < 0.5`), so a predicted roll-back at -1.9 m/s counts as a predicted stop.
result.next_step: Re-score the existing 40 checkpoints without retraining (the model/analyze harness is deterministic and takes a few minutes per run on the local GPU): (a) split the 'stop' class into stationary (status 'stall', or mean |vx| over the tail < 0.5 m/s) versus moving timeouts, i.e. fix `stuck_end` so 'crawl' exists; (b) report every pre-stop and in-stall test as per-episode agreement with Chrono at the same frame (pred < 0.5 vs recorded |vx| < 0.5) plus |pred-rec|, and change stall_eval's 'approach' term to |pred-rec| like 'matched'; (c) exclude resume events at frame <= 40 from 'recovery'. Then check whether the wp8_p6_k80_prog family still leads, whether over-holding (held-where-Chrono-moved) predicts each run's feasible-route rejection count, and re-derive the notes' 13.4 table from the corrected numbers before committing it.

findings.claim: The 47/52 gate+fastest result is exactly what the maximum of ~40 exchangeable noisy runs looks like; the true per-run effect is about +0.8 layout and the best run's extra +2 is selection noise, as the seed replicates and the sealed arenas confirm.
findings.evidence: Recomputed from artifacts/traverse/wp8_eval/<run>/imagine_f105/rows.json + artifacts/traverse/wp7_cache_v1/labels.json (all imagined-ok candidates ranked by mean commanded speed, fallback = fastest overall; note the 47 requires counting detour_*/slope_aware candidates by their mean_speed, excluding non-speed candidates gives 46). Distribution over 42 evaluated models: 43:1, 44:13, 45:24, 46:3, 47:1; wp8 runs mean 44.77, SD 0.72 vs heuristic 44. Exchangeable null (each layout's empirical feasible-pick rate across the 40 runs, independent draws): expected max over 40 = 46.5, P(max >= 47) = 0.51. The best run's 3 fixes / 0 breaks is an exact two-sided sign-test p = 0.25 even before selection. Same config, seeds 0/1/2: 47/45/45 on f105 -> 85/85/87 on the sealed f106+f107 (heuristic 86; recomputed from wp8_eval/<run>/imagine_sealed/rows.json + wp7_cache_sealed/labels.json, matching notes 13.5). The plain fine-tune wp7_ft_mix_amd also scores 45 on f105, i.e. the median stall-ablation run.

The +0.775 is the in-sample f105 mean and is almost entirely two layouts. arena_f105__s_hill3_hill1_t-60_sh is a CONTACT failure of the heuristic (seq_v8_8 completes in Chrono in 16.7 s with contact); 33/40 models reject it as an imagined timeout (img_time 30, not failed) — an unrelated reason — and 18/40 end up with a feasible pick there. arena_f105__x_hill3_h180 (fastest direct_v8 = Chrono timeout) is "fixed" by 9/40 runs only because the detour_R candidate (mean_speed 3.55) becomes eligible in the all-candidates variant; in the speed-only variant it is fixed by 0/40 and the mean effect drops to +0.5. verified.claim: The gate+fastest metric is structurally protected on this benchmark: false rejections almost never break the heuristic's pick, the fallback reverts to the heuristic whenever the model rejects everything, and the gate never abstains, so 'gate >= heuristic' is close to guaranteed regardless of model quality.
verified.evidence: Over 40 runs x 52 f105 layouts, models rejected a feasible fastest candidate 187 times and this broke the pick only 2 times (1.1%), because P(2nd-fastest feasible | fastest feasible) = 0.95 (bank feasibility by speed rank 0/1/2/3 = 0.85/0.83/0.90/0.83). The infeasible fastest was rejected in 98 of 320 opportunities and only 33.7% of those became fixes. Fallback (reject-all) fired on 1-8 layouts per run on f105 (8 for wp8_p6_k8) and 0-5 on the sealed set; the gate abstains on 0/13 no-solution layouts while the world-model own pick abstained on 0-2. A random rejecter with matched rejection rate scores 43.9 +- 0.7 (mean over 4000 sims), so the models' +0.8 is real discrimination (AUC 0.62-0.71 per summary.json) but small, and on the sealed set pooled over 5 runs it is 2 fixes / 2 breaks.

Evidence checks (40 wp8 runs x 52 layouts, all-candidates convention):

- Gate abstains 0/13 by construction. CONFIRMED. "Own pick abstained on 0-2": WRONG — distribution over 40 runs is 0:14, 1:11, 2:7, 3:4, 4:1, 5:2, 7:1 (pick_f105.txt: wp8b_k120_p9 7/13, wp8_p3_k80 5/13, wp8_p6_k8 5/13).
- Random rejecter with the same rejection count per run, 100 draws x 40 runs = 4000 sims: mean 43.93, sd 0.68, P(>=44) = 0.795, P(>44) = 0.146, range 40-47 (per-layout-matched variant: 44.16 +- 0.84). Models: mean 44.77 (+0.85 over matched random; sd over runs 0.72), 39/40 >= 44, 27/40 > 44. CONFIRMED, and the excess is (weakly) tied to model quality: corr(gate, auc_reject) = 0.28; top-20 AUC runs 45.00 vs bottom-20 44.55.

CONFIRMED (matches the notes 13.5 table).

Structural checks the claim under-states: without the fallback rule (nothing accepted = failure) the 40 runs average 43.17, only 16/40 reach >= 44 and 2/40 beat the heuristic — the fallback alone is worth +1.6 layouts, twice the +0.85 "discrimination" excess. Oracle gate (reject exactly the infeasible routes) = 52, i.e. the metric's headroom is +8; adversarial gate (reject exactly the feasible routes) = 15.

Where the interpretation overreaches: "close to guaranteed regardless of model quality" is not what the simulation shows. A zero-quality (random) rejecter at the models' rejection rates (7-48% of routes) scores 43.9 +- 0.7, i.e. BELOW the heuristic on average and below it in ~20% of draws (only 15% strictly above); at rejection rates 0.7/0.9 P(>=44) falls to 0.57/0.37 (mean 43.6/42.8); and the metric has no floor at the heuristic (15/52 possible). The models' 39/40 >= 44 and 27/40 > 44 exceed the random rates, which is exactly the small model-quality effect the claim's own +0.8 concedes. The accurate statement is compression, not a one-sided guarantee.
verdict.corrected_claim: On this benchmark the gate+fastest metric is heavily compressed rather than one-sidedly protected: because the bank's second-fastest route is feasible whenever the fastest is (42/44 on f105, 83/86 sealed), a false rejection of the feasible fastest breaks the pick only ~1% of the time (2 of 187 across the 40 wp8 runs), the fallback to the heuristic when nothing is accepted is worth +1.6 layouts on average (without it the 40 runs average 43.2/52 and only 2 beat the heuristic), and only 8 f105 / 7 sealed layouts can be fixed at all (oracle 52/52). Consequently any rejecter with the models' 7-48% rejection rates lands within about +-1 of the heuristic: a random rejecter at matched rate scores 43.9 +- 0.7 (P(>=44) = 0.80, P(>44) = 0.15), the 40 models average 44.8 (39/40 >= 44, 27/40 > 44), and the +0.8 excess is a real but small discrimination effect (corr with reject-AUC 0.28; f105 reject-AUC 0.53-0.70 across the 40 runs) that concentrates on one contact-failure layout (18 of 33 fixes) and one detour layout (9), and does not reproduce on the sealed set (2 fixes / 2 breaks pooled over 5 runs). "gate >= heuristic" is therefore the likely outcome for weakly-discriminating models with moderate rejection rates, not a guarantee independent of model quality: a random rejecter falls below the heuristic 20% of the time, high rejection rates (0.7-0.9) drop that to 43-63%, and an anti-discriminating rejecter can score 15/52. Own-pick abstention on the 13 no-solution layouts is 0-7 per run (not 0-2).
